analysis.title: Energy Fuels Inc. (UUUU): Donald project receives conditional approval for up to A$180mn of Australian government financing; FID by year-end
key_insights: On 10/26, UUUU announced that Export Finance Australia (EFA) and the National Reconstruction Fund Corporation (NRFC) conditionally approved up to A$180mn (US$126mn) of financing for Phase 1 of the Donald Rare Earth and Mineral Sands Project in Australia.

The A$180mn is part of a proposed A$200mn senior project finance debt facility. EFA and NRFC have conditionally approved up to A$70mn and A$110mn respectively, and commercial lenders are expected to provide the remaining A$20mn. The facilities are expected to have a 10-year tenor from financial close, priced at BBSY plus a margin.

Commitments remain subject to definitive documentation, due diligence, remaining debt funding and final approvals. Talks on the remaining commercial term loan and bank guarantee facilities are ongoing.

UUUU targets a final investment decision (FID) on Donald by year-end 2026. Astron has previously said FID was expected at the close of project financing negotiations, which GS cites as support for a year-end FID.

Donald is a fully permitted, shovel-ready rare earths and heavy mineral sands project in Victoria, Australia, developed through a JV between UUUU and Astron Limited. Phase 1 is expected to have a 40-year mine life and produce ~9,000 tpa of rare earth element concentrate (REEC) containing monazite and xenotime (including NdPr, Tb and Dy), plus ~225,000 tpa of heavy mineral concentrate.
Under the JV, UUUU is expected to buy all the REEC for downstream processing and Astron is expected to buy all the heavy mineral concentrate.

UUUU is earning a 49% interest in the JV by funding the first A$183mn (US$127mn) of upfront equity. It has invested ~A$60mn (US$41mn) so far, for a 15.3% interest, and must invest another ~A$86mn (US$60mn) and issue US$14mn of common shares to reach 49%.
Phase 1 capex is estimated (per Astron) at A$450mn (US$317mn).

UUUU plans to process the ~9,000 tpa of REEC at the White Mesa Mill into ~1,000 tpa of NdPr oxide plus Tb and Dy oxides. These would feed its metallization and alloying capacity acquired through ASM and, after the planned VAC acquisition, permanent magnet manufacturing.

Per the company, Donald's NdPr output could supply ~75% of the expanded ~3,600 tpa NdFeB alloy capacity at the Korean Metals Plant, and its REEC could support ~77% of VAC's existing magnet manufacturing capacity across US and European facilities.
GS is Not Rated on UUUU, with the rating and price target removed. The disclosures say Goldman Sachs is acting as financial advisor on an announced strategic matter involving Energy Fuels.

market_movers.rationale: GS is Not Rated on UUUU because it is advising on a strategic matter involving the company, so no rating or target applies. The note is an event update on the Donald financing approval.

earnings_insights: GS estimates for UUUU: revenue $65.9mn in 12/25 (reported), $146.1mn in 12/26E, $207.5mn in 12/27E and $280.8mn in 12/28E. EBITDA is $(95.7)mn in 12/25, $(52.0)mn in 12/26E, $(5.9)mn in 12/27E and $24.5mn in 12/28E.

GS EPS estimates: $(0.38) for 12/25, $(0.22) for 12/26E, $(0.04) for 12/27E and $(0.02) for 12/28E. Quarterly EPS was $(0.13) in 6/26 (reported) with estimates of $(0.02) for 9/26E, $(0.02) for 12/26E and $(0.01) for 3/27E.
risk_factors: The A$180mn commitments are conditional on definitive documentation, due diligence, remaining debt funding and final approvals.
The remaining A$20mn commercial term loan and bank guarantee facilities are still under negotiation.
FID is only targeted by year-end 2026, and UUUU must still fund ~A$86mn of equity plus issue US$14mn of shares to earn its 49% stake.
Phase 1 capex of A$450mn is an Astron estimate. The downstream magnet strategy depends on the planned VAC acquisition, which is not yet complete.
geopolitical: The note covers Australian government financing (Export Finance Australia and the National Reconstruction Fund Corporation) for a rare earths project that UUUU expects to be its first large-scale source of rare earth mineral feedstock for a US and European mine-to-magnet supply chain.
